### policy_self_consistency (this task only)

Charter-global conclusions this task rests on are cited, not restated:
`audits/policy_task/retrofit_projects_desk/_difficulty.md` — `### policy_conflict_scan`,
`### rule_compute_equivalence`, `### action_binding_and_uuids`, `### prerequisite_graph`,
`### prerequisite_sentences`, `### override_declarations`, `### factor_ladders`.

**Handling time.** Two writes, each evaluated on the world that holds at its own step.

- Step 1, `bill_storage_charge_e8c4e90e`: evaluated on `initial_state` at
  `frozen_time = 2026-06-18 10:20:00 America/Chicago` (`NOW = 2026-06-18`). Its policy declares
  `prerequisite: []`, so its moment is the opening world.
- Step 2, `settle_project_cancellation_6d1f2e6f`: evaluated on `initial_state` **plus** the
  synchronous effect of step 1 — the `retrofit_events` row `ctx.create(... event_type=
  "retrofit_progress_billed", billing_class="storage", amount_usd=…, due_date=today …)` written by
  `task_tools.py`. `billings_raised` sums `billing_class='storage'` among others, so the settlement
  must be computed after the storage line exists, never before. Nothing in this task is computed
  early: the storage charge reads no field the settlement writes, and the settlement reads the
  storage line the first step leaves.

**No real-world waits.** Every fact either gold write consumes is an authoritative record already in
`initial_state` (the project row, the two stored-chiller deliveries, the deposit billing and its
payment, the late-fee billing, the confirmed cancellation notice, the maintenance agreement at the
same site), the real DB effect of the preceding gold write of this same task (the storage line), or
a choice the customer states immediately (the reason for stopping; her own running of the
authorisation). No diagnosis, delivery, call-out, payment clearing, manual approval, third-party
processing, back-office batch, future date or cooling-off period stands between the two writes: the
storage charge is an agent write that completes in the call, and the settlement is the customer's own
write handed over in the same call.

**Charter-global defects bearing on this task.** Finding **F3** of `_difficulty.md`
(`stopped_stage_basis` labelled `method` while its tiers only substitute a rate) bears on this
task's `settlement_amount_usd`; the consequence is a false claim in `factors[].effect` and is

25 per cent into an otherwise unchanged formula. Findings F1, F2, F4 and observations O1–O4 bear on
task 1, not on this task. Observation **O5** (base's deposit-refund branch, undeclared) touches this
task's policy: it produces no second answer here, because the settlement (103446.25) is far larger
than the deposit billing (67000.00), so base's refund branch cannot fire and base's "deposits are
applied to the settlement" is honoured by the extended formula's subtraction of
`payments_received = 67000.00`.

### problem_chain

Walked from the policy and the world alone, before any GT was read.

**Root problem.** The customer asks to stop project `4ca039dc-270f-428f-98b7-5165e6079e31` and to
know what stopping it costs — that is `retrofit_ext_cancellation_settlement`
(`subject: retrofit_project_cancelled`, `computes: settlement_amount_usd`,
`target_tool: settle_project_cancellation_6d1f2e6f`, `owner="user"`).

**Prerequisite sentences the root problem's own rule carries.** One, and only one:

> "The settlement figure on a stopped project is worked out only once every week the delivered
> equipment has stood in storage is carried as a storage charge on the project's billing record."

**Is that state true at `frozen_time`?** No. Filtering
`initial_state.retrofit_events` on `project_id = 4ca039dc-…` and
`event_type = retrofit_progress_billed` gives exactly three rows —
`b92f12f6-…` (`billing_class: deposit`, 67000.00, due 2026-03-07) and
`b142b2ab-…` (`billing_class: late_fee`, 837.50, due 2026-04-18); there is **no** row with
`billing_class = 'storage'` on this project at all. Meanwhile
`50a57032-…` and `2c2d745e-…` (`event_type: retrofit_equipment_delivered`,
`stored_off_site: "stored"`, `delivered_date: 2026-04-22`) show two chillers standing in storage.
So weeks have been stood and nothing is carried on the billing record: the prerequisite is genuinely
unmet at the opening, not an eligibility already satisfied.

**Which write brings that state about?** Reading the other policies' own rules, the only one whose
result is a charge on equipment a building cannot yet receive is
`retrofit_ext_storage_accrual_billing` ("The storage charge raised on equipment a building cannot yet
receive is worked out from the weeks the equipment has stood in storage …"), and in the whole tool
module only `bill_storage_charge_e8c4e90e` creates a `billing_class="storage"` line
(`task_tools.py`, first function body). One reading; no second candidate.

**Does that problem carry prerequisites of its own?** Its rule carries no sentence joining its result
to anything else in an ordering connective (see `_difficulty.md`, `### prerequisite_sentences`), and
its `prerequisite` is `[]`. The walk terminates.

**Tree.**

```
retrofit_ext_cancellation_settlement          (root, owner=user, settle_project_cancellation_6d1f2e6f)
   ^ value_input, gate billings_raised, form state
retrofit_ext_storage_accrual_billing          (owner=agent, bill_storage_charge_e8c4e90e)
```

- n = 1 prerequisite problem (within the 1–3 bound); `value_input` edges = 1 ≥ max(n−1, 1) = 1.
- Topological order: storage charge, then cancellation settlement. Acyclic.
- **At least one problem is the customer's own write:** the root is
  `settle_project_cancellation_6d1f2e6f`, declared `@tool(owner="user", rw="write")`, and the
  persona hands it over passively at the agent's direction ("When the agent hands the authorisation
  across to her she runs it herself and says it has gone through").

**Per-edge load-bearing run.** Skipping the storage write and replaying the settlement on the
otherwise unchanged opening world gives **102928.75**; with the storage write it gives
**103446.25**. The edge moves the scored parameter by exactly the storage charge (517.50). The edge
bears weight.

**Parallel edges.** The tree has a single edge, so there is no pair of out-edges to order and no
second defensible terminal state.

**No-wait argument.** `bill_storage_charge_e8c4e90e` reads only rows already in `initial_state` and
writes immediately; the customer is on the line and consents in advance ("If the agent tells her
something has to go onto the project's account before the figure can be settled, she says that is
fine, go ahead"). Nothing waits on an external event.

**The tool layer judges no prerequisite.** `task_tools.py`: `bill_storage_charge_e8c4e90e` does
`rows = ctx.find("retrofit_projects", project_id=project_id)` and, if the project exists, creates the
line — no check of storage weeks, no check of a free period, no refusal.
`settle_project_cancellation_6d1f2e6f` likewise does only the `ctx.find` existence check before
creating the settlement line and setting `status="cancelled"` — it never inspects whether a storage
charge stands on the billing record, never errors and never hints. The decision stays with the agent.

**Isomorphic to the tree the author declared?** The `prerequisite` block of
`retrofit_ext_cancellation_settlement` declares exactly this one edge, with this `kind`, `form`,
`gate`, `resolved_by` and `policy_source` — see `_difficulty.md`, `### prerequisite_graph`. The tree
the auditor derived from the policy and the world alone is the same tree.

### task_independent_derivation

**Now / wait / refuse: act now.** The owner asks for the project to be stopped and settled on this
call. Every base eligibility that could bar it is satisfied or silent:
`retrofit_cancellation_and_settlement` carries `eligibility: []`; the project is live
(`status: "scheduled"`, not `closed`, `cancelled` or `declined`); the cancellation is the owner's own
and is evidenced by a confirmed written notice (`retrofit_requests.004868eb-…`,
`request_type: cancellation_notice`, `outcome: confirmed`, `notice_date: 2026-06-09`), so it is not a
company stoppage for non-payment. Nothing in the policy defers the settlement to a future date.

**Need, authorisation and timing, from `user_scenario` alone.** The object is named (the chiller
project at Kestrel Court, confirmed by `purchase_order_ref: "PO-2026-0418"` which she reads out); the
timing is named ("settled on this call, today"); the authorisation boundary is named twice and in
both directions — the office's own side is delegated ("she is content for the desk to work the figure
out and to do whatever the contract says the office has to do on its own side") while the stopping
itself is reserved to her ("she will do the stopping herself … she is not letting anyone else press
that button for her"). That matches the owners exactly: the storage line is an
`owner="agent"` write, the settlement an `owner="user"` write. She raises **only** the root problem;
she never names, hints at or asks after a storage charge, and her one conditional reaction
("If the agent tells her something has to go onto the project's account …") is passive and names
nothing. She issues no other item of work — no document to send, no address, no statement — and she
closes at the settlement ("Once she hears the project is stopped and settled she thanks them … and
rings off").

**Context closure.** Identity is reachable: company name and phone volunteered, `account_number`
"650142" and `tax_id_last4` "5518" on request, all matching `customers.173fa4f8-…`. Every policy
input is reachable through the runtime share tools —
`find_retrofit_projects` (the project row: variant, status, dates, contract value, site),
`find_retrofit_events` (deliveries, billings, payments),
`find_retrofit_requests` (the cancellation notice; and the absence of any schedule request),
`find_maintenance_agreements` (the agreement at the same site) — and the cancellation reason is a
definite persona answer. No field needed for the answer is visible only in the raw seed.

**The object.** The narrowest business object is the single project
`4ca039dc-270f-428f-98b7-5165e6079e31` at site `4575fe8c-…` (Kestrel Court), variant
**Energy Retrofit Project**, `contract_value_usd = 268000.00`. Correlation key: `project_id`. The
owner's other project `04f36290-…` (Halstead Commons, Equipment Replacement Order, `status: closed`)
is excluded throughout — its deposit 9250.00, its late fee 138.75, its completion billing 9250.00 and
its three payments belong to a different `project_id`, and base `retrofit_agg_multi_holding` says in
terms that "nothing is pooled between projects".

stood in storage is carried as a storage charge on the project's billing record", so the settlement
is evaluated after the storage line and before the cancellation is written.

### factor_weight

Every figure below is the auditor's own recomputation on this task's handling-time world.

**Computation 1 — `storage_amount_usd` (gold 517.50), 4 declared factors.**

| factor | effect | tiers genuinely differ in that kind? | tier taken and the records that put the customer on it | what `baseline.rule` states for that input | `baseline` encodes it? | scored value under that baseline |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `storage_clock_anchor` | `method` | yes — three different dates anchor the same week count | tier 1, "the equipment arrived before the day installation was booked to begin and that booked day has already passed": `delivered_date 2026-04-22` (rows `50a57032-…`, `2c2d745e-…`) against `scheduled_start_date 2026-06-01` and `NOW 2026-06-18` | "The storage clock runs from the day the equipment arrived" → `stored_since` | yes (`clock_start: stored_since`) | **3622.50** |
| `free_period_allowance` | `parameter` | yes — 3 / 2 / 1 weeks | tier 2, an active agreement **and** a late fee inside twelve months: `maintenance_agreements.0f548db7-…` `status: "active"`, `site_id 4575fe8c-…` (**another difficulty's holding**), with `retrofit_events.b142b2ab-…` `billing_class: "late_fee"`, `due_date 2026-04-18` | "One week of storage is free" → `K('base_free_weeks') = 1` | yes | **1035.00** |
| `storage_rate_premium` | `parameter` | yes — 345 / 270 / 225 | tier 1, a chiller at the rented laydown yard: `equipment_type: "chiller"` on the stored deliveries | "The weekly storage rate is the project's weekly storage charge" → `P('storage_fee_per_week_usd') = 225` | yes | **337.50** |
| `lot_bay_scaling` | `method` | yes — × unit count / × the shared-bay factor / unscaled | tier 2, two units in storage: two rows with `stored_off_site: "stored"` | "The weekly charge for the lot is the weekly storage rate as it stands" → `weekly_rate` | yes | **345.00** |

- Whole-baseline fall-back: **1800.00** — definite, and different from gold.
- **Stamp check:** no field of any row names a free period, a storage tier or a weekly rate. The one
  field that looks like an outcome name, `retrofit_projects.last_change_type = "schedule_moved"`
  (with `last_change_date 2026-03-02`), **disagrees** with the tier: it would tempt a reader toward
  the "owner asked for the start to be moved" tier, but `retrofit_requests` holds no
  `schedule_request` at all, and that tier additionally requires arrival on or after the booked day,
  which is false. It is a decoy, not a shortcut.
- **Near-miss:** `retrofit_events.eb02e86a-…` — a **pump** delivered 2026-04-10 with
  `stored_off_site: "delivered_to_site"`. A careless reader counts it as a third unit in storage
  (moving `lot_bay_scaling` to the ×3 tier) and as the earliest arrival (moving the clock to
  2026-04-10). It is excluded by the rule's own words — the ladders speak of "units … standing in
  storage" and "the lot standing in storage", and this lot went to site.
- Counts for this computation: 4 factors (within 4–6), 2 `parameter`, 2 `method`; multi-source:
  `free_period_allowance` and `storage_clock_anchor`; cross-difficulty: `free_period_allowance`
  (`maintenance`), whose holding row is present in `initial_state` and consistent with that product's
  own charter (variant "Preventive Maintenance Agreement", `status: "active"`, term 2024-09-01 to
  2027-08-31, covering `NOW`).

**Computation 2 — `settlement_amount_usd` (gold 103446.25), 5 declared factors.**

| factor | effect | tiers genuinely differ in that kind? | tier taken and the records that put the customer on it | what `baseline.rule` states for that input | `baseline` encodes it? | scored value under that baseline |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `stopped_stage_basis` | `method` **(mislabelled — see `_difficulty.md` F3)** | the tiers differ, but only as 55 / 25 / 8 per cent into one unchanged formula | tier 2: `equipment_released_date "2026-02-20"` present, `mobilization_date ""` absent | "The stage of a stopped project is the stage it reached after award and before the equipment order was released" → `P('cancellation_fee_pct_awarded') = 8` | yes | **69276.25** |
| `notice_lead_relief` | `method` | yes — the computed stage fee is scaled by ½, ¾ or not at all | tier 2: a confirmed written notice (`004868eb-…`, `notice_date 2026-06-09`) reaching the office after the booked start `2026-06-01` | "the stage fee is the contract value multiplied by the project's cancellation fee for that stage, rounded to the nearest cent" → `RND(268000 × stage_pct/100, 2)` | yes | **120196.25** |
| `equipment_share_of_value` | `parameter` | yes — 65 / 55 / 50 per cent | tier 1: latest delivery `equipment_type: "chiller"` | "The equipment released to the supplier is valued at the equipment share of the contract value, which is half" → `K('default_equipment_share_pct') = 50` | yes | **91386.25** |
| `restocking_return_window` | `parameter` | yes — `P+10` / `P` / none | tier 1: stored equipment arrived 2026-04-22, i.e. 57 days before the stop day | "the restocking fee applied is the project's own restocking fee" → `P('restocking_fee_pct') = 20` | yes | **86026.25** |
| `late_fee_settlement_treatment` | `method` | yes — which late-fee rows enter the settlement and at what weight | tier 2: exactly one late fee on the project (`b142b2ab-…`, 837.50) | "the settlement carries the billings raised together with every late fee raised on the project in full" → `billings_raised + late_fees_raised` | yes | **103865.00** |

- Whole-baseline fall-back: **49595.00** — definite, and different from gold.
- **Stamp check:** `cancellation_stage` and `cancellation_reason` are empty on the record at the
  opening (the tool fills them), and no field names a stage percentage, an equipment share or a
  restocking rate. The nearest thing to an outcome stamp, `balance_due = 837.50`, is the late fee
  alone and agrees with no tier.
- **Near-misses:** (a) the same pump delivery of 2026-04-10 — taking the *first* delivery instead of
  the latest gives `released_type = "pump"` and the 50 per cent default share; excluded by "the
  equipment delivered on the project" read at the latest `delivered_date`. (b) the whole of the
  **closed** Halstead Commons project `04f36290-…`, whose own late fee (138.75, due 2025-06-03),
  deposit (9250.00), completion billing (9250.00) and three payments a reader who aggregates by
  customer would fold in — counting two late fees would move `late_fee_settlement_treatment` to its
  third tier; excluded by base `retrofit_agg_multi_holding` ("Each project holds its own contract
  value, retainage and change allowance, and nothing is pooled between projects").
- Counts for this computation: 5 factors (within 4–6), 2 `parameter`, 3 `method` as labelled
  (2 `parameter` / 3 `method` claimed; on the honest labelling of F3, 3 `parameter` / 2 `method` —
  the floors of 2 `parameter` and 1 `method` hold either way); multi-source: `notice_lead_relief`
  and `restocking_return_window`; cross-difficulty: none in this computation, which is why the
  task-level floor is carried by `free_period_allowance` above.

**Task-level bounds.** Over both computations: 9 declared factors, every one proved to bear weight
above; at least one multi-source factor (four of them) and at least one cross-difficulty factor
(`free_period_allowance`, reading `maintenance`) whose other-product rows are seeded. Both floors met.

## findings

---

**R1 — `SOURCE-CHAIN RED` — a false world-assertion in `prerequisite_closure.edge_load_bearing`**

- **Symptom.** The closure states the terminal project balance under the counterfactual in which the
  storage billing is skipped as **104285.00**. Recomputed on the world that sentence names for
  itself, the balance is **103766.25**.
- **Root cause.** The counterfactual balance was asserted rather than replayed: the scored settlement
  under the skip (102928.75) is correct and the storage line is correctly said to be absent, but the
  two were not added to the opening balance. `retrofit_projects.4ca039dc-….balance_due` opens at
  837.50; `settle_project_cancellation_6d1f2e6f` adds the settlement to it and nothing else is
  written, so the balance is `837.50 + 102928.75 = 103766.25`.
- **Evidence.**
  - `tasks/0.json`, `prerequisite_closure.edge_load_bearing[0].skipped_effect`: "… and the scored
    settlement_amount_usd 102928.75 instead of 103446.25; the terminal state also loses the storage
    billing row and the project balance ends at 104285.00 instead of 104801.25."
  - `initial_state.retrofit_projects.4ca039dc-270f-428f-98b7-5165e6079e31.balance_due = 837.5`.
  - `task_tools.py`, `settle_project_cancellation_6d1f2e6f`:
    `balance = round(float(project.get("balance_due") or 0) + amount, 2)` — the only balance movement
    on the skipped path.
  - Replaying the skip: settlement 102928.75, balance `837.50 + 102928.75 = 103766.25`. The gold path
    is stated correctly (104801.25 = 837.50 + 517.50 + 103446.25) and was independently confirmed, so
    the error is confined to the counterfactual.
- **Demonstrated consequence.** A sentence of the proof asserts what the world is like and
  contradicts the recomputation by 518.75. The conclusion it is offered in support of — that the edge
  bears weight — is independently true (the scored settlement moves by exactly the storage charge,
  517.50, which the auditor verified before the reveal), so the tree itself holds; what fails is the
  proof as written.
- **Affected artifact and location.**
  `env/env_0002_commercial_hvac_service_contractor/tasks/retrofit_projects_desk/tasks/0.json`,
  `prerequisite_closure.edge_load_bearing[0].skipped_effect`, last clause. No scored parameter, no
  gold argument and no terminal state of the gold path is affected.
- **Relation to previous revisions.** First revision.

---

**Charter-global findings bearing on this task**, recorded once in
`audits/policy_task/retrofit_projects_desk/_difficulty.md` and cited here rather than restated:
**F3** (`SOURCE-FACTOR RED`, `stopped_stage_basis` labelled `method` while its tiers only substitute
a rate — it decides this task's `stage_pct`, 25 per cent on tier 2); observation **O5** (base's
deposit-refund branch undeclared, producing no second answer on this world). F1, F2, F4 and
observations O1–O4, O6, O7 bear on task 1 or on no task world.
